# 1.2.57 - tests that measure what they say

The first of the stages that lead to 1.3.0 "Stained Update". Each stage ships
on its own as the next 1.2.X, and this one comes first because every stage
after it leans on the tests: most of what changed here is how the module
checks itself, plus four holes those checks turned up. Nothing here asks a
world to be migrated.

## Fixed

- **A player could raise a GM ruling card in somebody else's name.** The
  Hope Call and Dynamic action requests did not check that the character they
  named belonged to the player who sent them. They do now.
- **Project progress from a player now has to be for a project that player
  can see.** A player who knew the id of a secret project could fill its bar
  from outside it. The progress is also credited to the player who really
  sent it, not to whoever the request claimed.
- **Only the player holding an object can tie its trace to a murder.**
- **`game.drpg.runTests({ tier: 1 })` really is safe during play now.** Five
  of its checks opened and closed the Class Trial on the live world, and one
  walked a student into a room sixty-one times, which fires an armed trap.
  They no longer do, and tier 1 now checks at the end that nothing in the world
  moved - and names what did, if something did.
- **`game.drpg.fileSizes()` lists every stylesheet and the Polish file.** It
  left out four of the six stylesheets.

## New

- **A warning when Daggerheart is newer than the version this module was
  checked on.** A GM sees it once per Daggerheart version and can silence it
  for that version. It also names any place the module hooks into Daggerheart
  that it could no longer find. Newer versions still load.
- **Daggerheart 2.6.5 is now the minimum** (it was 2.6.0, which nobody had
  tested). 2.6.5 is the version the module is verified on.

## Daggerheart 2.10.5

Daggerheart 2.10.5 is out, and this release is still verified on 2.6.5 only.
A read of the source changes between the two (`audit/probe-daggerheart-2.10.5.md`)
found one thing that breaks: since Daggerheart 2.9.0, changing or deleting an
item on a character deletes the Actions resource this module adds (read in the
source, not yet seen at a table). It is scheduled for a later stage, together with three
things the same read marked as at risk. If you are on 2.10.x, the warning
above will tell you so; the module has not yet been run on it at a table.

## For people working on the module

- The suite's "skipped" now only ever means a fact about where it runs (no
  layout, no canvas, no CSS cascade, no Daggerheart sheets). About a dozen
  tests used to decide whether to skip by looking at the module's own result.
  One of them skipped because the world had music switched off, not because
  there was no audio; it measures now.
- The headless harness draws the dialog windows the suite reads. Eleven tests
  that failed there and passed in Foundry now run for real: 266 passed, 0
  failed apart from the version stamp this release fixes, 16 skipped.
- The headless harness delivers every chat message to every client, as
  Foundry v14 does, so its privacy checks now read what a player's browser
  actually receives. That found two leaks, both already scheduled for later
  stages: what a Search found is readable from a player's console, and the
  killer's opening roll reaches everyone's browser with the killer's name on
  it.
- The release workflow refuses branches other than `main`, takes a title,
  checks that the README and the six handbooks name the version, and
  publishes a manifest that installs its own zip rather than the newest one.
- One `npm ci` step in `audit/harness`, and the harness runs from any clone.
